text:
The coulombic force between two point charges $q_1$ and $q_2$ separated by a distance $r$ is given by Coulomb's law:
$$F = \frac{k |q_1 q_2|}{r^2}$$

By Newton's third law of motion, the magnitude of the force exerted by charge $+3\mu\text{C}$ on $-4\mu\text{C}$ is equal to the magnitude of the force exerted by $-4\mu\text{C}$ on $+3\mu\text{C}$. Therefore, the ratio of the magnitudes of coulombic forces acting on them is always **$1:1$**.

None of the given non-blank options (A, B, D) equal $1:1$, and Option (C) is blank (it likely originally represented $1:1$).
